body:
Path: records — Undo restores the value the record had | 缺项 (the Undo snapshot of a written lookup is taken from a `$expand`ed row, so Undo writes the related record object into the reference slot instead of its id) | P1

## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p1` · `domain:ui` · `area:records` · `pm:queue`. Direction: normalise at the one capture rule, from the object's field map, so all three surfaces are fixed together

Triage: lands in `@object-ui/core`'s `captureUpdateUndoData` (the one capture rule the runner, the console runtime and the record page share since PR objectui#11121) ⇒ `domain:ui`.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T17:54Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why p1.** NORTH-STAR rule 1, data integrity.
- Under the server's default lenient value-shape posture, the Undo write is admitted, and the lookup slot then stores an object. That is silent corruption, of exactly the kind `os migrate value-shapes` exists to find.
- Under the strict posture it is refused, and Undo fails loudly. That is the milder case.
- **The reach is taught.** objectstack's published skill example `ReassignLeadAction` is an undoable `api` action that writes a lookup. On the grid, any written lookup that is also a visible or grouping column is captured the same way.

**Direction.**
- `captureUpdateUndoData`, or one sibling that all three callers run first, captures a **reference-bearing** written field's stored id when the row holds an expanded value (the value's id, through the adapter's id key).
- "Reference-bearing" is read from **the object's field map** (`isExpandableFieldType`). ⛔ Never a shape heuristic: a `json` field may legitimately hold an object with an `id`.
- ⛔ No per-surface fix: the rule is shared precisely so that one change covers the runner, the console runtime and the record page.
- **Pins:**
  - On the record page and on a grid row, Undo of a lookup update restores the id (`'a1'`).
  - A `json` field holding `{ id, … }` restores the object unchanged.
  - The objectui#10404 / objectui#11082 pins stay green.
- **Coordinate:** objectui#11081 (p1, the keyboard listener on the same undo path) is a different file. Whichever lands second rebases.

Claim: PM loop round 4 — `domain:ui` execution seat 2

Worktree: `objectui-issue-11122`
Domain: `domain:ui`
Seat: `domain:ui#2`
File surface (triage `5895671250`: normalise at the one capture rule, from the object's field map):
- `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`: `captureUpdateUndoData` (`:957`), or one sibling that all three callers run first, captures a reference-bearing written field's stored id when the row holds an expanded value. The runner's own call is at `:1674`.
- "Reference-bearing" is read from the object's field map through `isExpandableFieldType` (`packages/core/src/utils/expand-fields.ts:202`). ⛔ Never a shape heuristic.
- The two other callers, which pass the field map in: `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` (`:543`, `:556`) and `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` (`:989`, `:1002`).
- Pins:
  - Undo of a lookup update restores the id on the record page and on a grid row.
  - A `json` field holding `{ id, … }` restores the object unchanged.
  - The objectui#10404 / objectui#11082 pins stay green.
- One changeset.
Stop on breach; explain in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (TIER_DEFAULT; `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` over this surface: no path-derived mandate, at objectstack `288611e3`)
Clause-②: no
Why no: an Undo snapshot's value changes from an expanded object to the stored id. `captureUpdateUndoData` may gain a field-map parameter, which widens nothing a caller can author and moves no schema, prop or accepted set.

PR objectui#11086 touches `core/src/actions/actionKeys.ts` only, which is disjoint. objectui#11080 (queued, `AppContent` undo toasts) is disjoint by file.
